# workflow: # The inventory of what this pipeline actually grades, and the manifest that keeps it from
# going stale. Every named step in base.yml, php.yml and js.yml has a row; `gates.sh`
# fails when the workflows contain a step this file does not, so a gate added to the
# pipeline cannot escape the inventory in silence. Same idiom as scaffold/seeds.tsv in
# rak200/workflow: the manifest is what makes it a seed.
# Written because reconciling by hand does not hold. RFC 0017 step 0 read the pipeline on
# 2026-08-12 and found the canary list was "about to fire eight shots at a target that has
# changed shape", putting the real inventory at roughly seventeen. Thirteen days later it
# was wrong again. A list maintained beside the thing it describes drifts from it; a list
# class    gate       its failure means the REPOSITORY is wrong — the thing a canary fires at
#          report     runs a tool and records the result WITHOUT gating; a separate step
#                     grades it. Called out rather than folded into `gate` because a report
#                     that silently stops working is the estate's own `looks green, enforces
#                     nothing` shape, and it is invisible by construction: the step is green
#          setup      its failure means the RUNNER or the network is wrong, not the repo
#          aggregate  republishes other jobs' results; the required check `ci / gate`
# A `gate` row is a canary owed. `report`, `setup` and `aggregate` rows are not — but the
# step that grades a `report` is, and it is the one worth firing at, because a green report
# and a green grader are indistinguishable from a working control.

step: Every workflow the seeds pin is callable
The gate inventory matches the workflows
Seeded files match the pinned scaffold
The pinned scaffold is not obsolete
The pinned pipeline is not obsolete
README mirror badges match their sources
A repository with src/ has docs/
The PR title is a Conventional Commit
README PHPStan badge matches the effective level
README mirror badges match their sources
